headline: Oil fell about 6% before the open on Iran peace talk reports, with WTI under $100, and stock futures rose; Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum, and the put screen found one idea, an APH Dec 18 $72.50 put.
summary: The dashboard is current on Friday Oct 30 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-30), and Massive's Oct 30 closes match it; Brazil's market is closed today. At 8:55am ET Brent for January was $106.54, down 6.07%, and WTI $97.65, down 6.2%, after reports that Iran's supreme leader gave the government some authority to hold peace talks; US strike planning for after Tuesday's vote is still reported (CNBC). Before the open S&P 500 futures were up 0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures 0.8% and Dow futures 305 points (CNBC). Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all stock deal valued at $115 billion, and Oracle sold $10 billion of new stock (CNBC). Apple and Palantir report after the close, the RBA decides tonight at 10:30pm ET, the midterms are tomorrow, and NICE, PODD, RELY, AFRM and ZTS report Wednesday and Thursday. The weekday put screen checked all ten 'Buy zone now' names: only APH passes.

regime.why: Friday closed risk off, but this morning the two biggest worries both eased a little: oil fell about 6% on peace talk reports and tech futures bounced. The risk days are still ahead: the vote Tuesday, a possible strike window from Wednesday, three central bank decisions this week and the jobs report Friday. A morning bounce after the worst Nasdaq month since March 2025 is not yet a change in trend.

signals.title: Oil fell about 6% and WTI broke under $100 on reports that Iran's leader opened the door to peace talks
signals.since_yesterday: The talk turned into a price move: Brent fell 6.07% to $106.54 and WTI 6.2% to $97.65 by 8:55am ET, after reports that Iran's supreme leader gave the government some authority to negotiate.
signals.what_happened: Oil slid through the night: Brent was down 3.02% at $110.01 at 1:20am ET, then extended losses after reports that Iran's supreme leader granted the government some authority to hold peace talks; by 8:55am ET Brent for January was $106.54 and WTI for December $97.65 (CNBC). Rubio said Trump 'hasn't made a decision' and 'would prefer to do it peacefully' (CNBC). Iranian officials said a deal is still possible after the Qatar mediated talks if demands are met in practice (Al Jazeera via CNBC). The Wall Street Journal and New York Times still report the US is preparing for possible strikes after the Nov 3 vote, and Khamenei on Saturday ordered an 'immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted response' to any threat (CNBC). In Europe, oil and gas stocks led losses at the open, down 1.25% (CNBC).
signals.so_what: Last week traders were positioned long oil into the vote; a peace headline makes them sell fast, which is why the drop is this big. Who gains: airlines, truckers and anyone paying for diesel; it also eases the inflation fear that has three central banks leaning toward hikes. Who loses: refiners and drillers, whose windfall was built on scarcity. What would make this wrong: one strike or one tanker hit after Tuesday puts the whole move back. Both sides are still preparing for strikes, so this is a headline move, not a settled peace.
signals.for_you: Swing: the XOM (Oct 30 close 187.25, entry 169.99) and CVX (235.52, entry 218.23) swing plans are past their 2R targets; today's drop is the reason to take the target or at least move the stop to the entry before the open. COP (154.03, target 154.23) and EOG (165.54, target 167.48) have not reached target on a close; keep their stops (135.75, 147.98) and do not add. Airlines: DAL is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (lower highs and lower lows) and UAL is Avoid; no buy or put on a one day oil drop.

signals.title: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for $115 billion in stock; both fell premarket
signals.since_yesterday: The deal is signed: 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share, Lumentum holders get about 33% of the company.
signals.what_happened: Marvell will buy Lumentum in an all stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt. Lumentum holders get 4.5 Marvell shares per share, about 33% of the combined company. Marvell expects more than $1 billion of yearly cost savings, a $550 billion addressable market and higher earnings in the first year after closing (Marvell release via CNBC). On Oct 30 closes (MRVL 196.40, LITE 840.70) the offer is worth about 883.80 a Lumentum share, 5.1% above LITE's close (my calculation, Massive). Before the open MRVL was at 192.16, down 2.16%, and LITE down about 4% (CNBC). MRVL has fallen about 22% since talks were first reported (CNBC).
signals.so_what: Optics is the chokepoint inside AI clusters, and Marvell is paying a full price to own it. Marvell holders pay with dilution, so its stock fell; Lumentum's small premium means its price now moves with Marvell's. At premarket prices the offer is worth about 864.72 against LITE near 805, a gap of about 7%, which usually means traders see risk that approval takes long or fails. Second order: Coherent is now the largest independent laser maker left, and a $115 billion price puts a value on it. What would make this wrong: a regulator blocks the deal, or AI spenders cut optics orders.
signals.for_you: Long term: MRVL is Wait and under its 218.02 to 249.86 zone; LITE is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (it fell more than 8% in a month) and is now a buyout target, so the dashboard keeps it off the Lineup. No buy or put in either. COHR has no verdict here; watch only. Inbox: her long term scan added LITE today; that is a pre deal signal, ignore it.

It fell 3.4% on Oct 30 on about 1.37 times normal volume, and the rich put premium says traders expect more swings. That is the trade off: high pay for real risk. Its debt check passes and its next report is Jan 27, 2027 (dashboard). What would make this wrong: AI spenders cut rack orders, or APH closes under about 67.72, the dashboard's thesis line.

signals.title: AI funding strain: Oracle sold $10 billion of stock, and Kioxia warned flash memory prices are stalling
signals.what_happened: Oracle offered $10 billion of new common stock on Monday through Wells Fargo, Citigroup, BNP Paribas and others, and was down more than 2.5% premarket (CNBC, SEC 424B5). Kioxia fell about 14% after saying NAND flash selling prices rose in the mid 20% range in July to September, against 70% the quarter before, and guiding quarterly operating profit to 2 trillion yen against 2.35 trillion expected (CNBC). Even so, Micron was up 2.7%, Nvidia 1.5% and AMD 2.2% premarket (CNBC). ORCL closed at 130.67 on Oct 30 and MU at 884.74 (Massive).
signals.so_what: Last week the market punished spenders that burn cash. Oracle's answer is to sell stock, which spreads the cost to its holders and confirms that the AI build now needs outside money. Kioxia's warning is the first sign that flash memory prices, not just spender budgets, may be peaking. DRAM and HBM, which Micron sells, are still described as tight into 2028, so this cuts hardest at SNDK and WDC. What would make this wrong: Apple and Nvidia report strong demand and memory prices hold.
signals.for_you: No action. ORCL is Wait and closed under its 137.19 to 160.60 zone; no buy into a stock sale. No memory trades this week. A green premarket after a 6.5% October drop in the Nasdaq 100 is not a reason to chase.

signals.title: Asia's Monday: Korea bounced 2.24%, China rose on market support talk, Japan slipped
signals.what_happened: The KOSPI rose 2.24% to 5,859.08 after opening down 1.39%; the Nikkei fell 0.33% to 63,081.86; the Shanghai Composite rose 1.08% to 3,638.03 and the CSI 300 0.79% after reports that Chinese regulators will meet banks and brokers on steps to support stocks; the ASX 200 fell 0.58% (CNBC). CNBC's text said the Nikkei gained 0.33% and the KOSPI 2.38%; its own index levels give a 0.33% loss and a 2.24% gain, and the levels are used here.
signals.so_what: Korea's bounce follows Friday's 3.48% drop and the US futures rebound; it is a relief day, not a reversal, while foreign money has been leaving. China's move is policy talk on top of a 49.3 factory index; support talk tends to lift prices for days without fixing demand.
signals.for_you: No action. No Korea, Taiwan or memory trades this week. Chinese ADRs are not on the buy lists.

signals.title: Europe's factories keep growing, which raises the odds of a Bank of England hike Thursday
signals.what_happened: The eurozone manufacturing PMI was 52.7 in October, down from a four year high of 52.9 but above the 52.4 forecast; S&P Global said defense spending and stock building drive the strongest run in more than four years (CNBC). UK factory output grew at its fastest rate in more than two years, and S&P Global's Rob Dobson said it would 'further shorten the odds of interest rate hikes' from the BoE (CNBC). The Stoxx 600 was flat after the open (CNBC). The US ISM manufacturing index comes out at 10am ET (7am Pacific); no reliable consensus was found.
signals.so_what: Growth that holds up while oil is high keeps inflation sticky, so central banks keep leaning toward hikes. Defense spending is now showing up in factory data, which supports the European defense supply chain.
signals.for_you: No action. Puts must still beat the 4.927% 10 year. Watch the ISM at 7am Pacific: a hot number would cut into this morning's bounce.

signals.title: Midterms tomorrow: Democrats are expected to take the House, with the Senate uncertain
signals.since_yesterday: CNBC's sector read: a Democratic House means more oversight, and contractors and Medicaid insurers are the most exposed.
signals.what_happened: Democrats are expected to take control of the House on Tuesday while Senate control is uncertain (CNBC). CNBC says a Democratic win could bring tougher oversight of big companies and shift federal spending, naming Lockheed Martin for contracts, Molina and Centene for Medicaid funding, and crypto rules that are not yet locked into law. It also notes stocks have often done well under divided government, while analysts caution against counting on it.
signals.so_what: A split Congress usually means fewer new laws, which markets often like, but more hearings and budget fights. Health insurers that live on Medicaid carry the most direct risk; defense backlogs are long, so the effect there is slow. Results come in overnight Eastern time, and the Iran strike window opens right after.
signals.for_you: Swing: keep size small into Wednesday. No new puts on defense or managed care into the vote. LMT stays 'Accumulate on pullback' far above its zone.

signals.title: Smart money: Japan's largest life insurer keeps buying Corebridge; Congress is quiet
signals.what_happened: Nippon Life, a 10% owner of Corebridge Financial (CRBG), bought 4,658,665 shares from Oct 5 to Oct 23 for about $160 million (13D/A signed Oct 27) and more on Oct 26 at about $34.95, under a trading plan adopted Aug 7 (SEC Form 4). No Congress leader trades: the newest House filings are Oct 29, for trades on Oct 15 (4 and 18 days old), and the Senate feed still fails.
signals.so_what: A strategic owner adding under a plan set in August is a long term stake build, not a timing signal; it is weaker evidence than a CEO buying in the open market. It does show a big Japanese insurer wants more US annuity exposure while rates are high.
signals.for_you: Watch only. CRBG has no verdict, theme or setup.

history.when: January 17, 1991, the start of Desert Storm
history.what: NYMEX crude had its biggest one day drop on record, falling almost $11 to $21.44 a barrel, as the war began and the IEA planned to release 2.5 million barrels a day from stocks (Oil and Gas Journal).
history.lesson: War premiums can vanish in a day once the market thinks the worst is known. Traders who wait for certainty give back their gains first.

source.title: Oil prices log record plunge despite war start (Oil and Gas Journal, January 1991)

cycle.differences: In 1991 the war itself removed the fear, and strategic stocks flooded in. Today it is only talk of peace, while both sides still prepare for strikes, and the shortage is in refined fuel and safe passage, which takes longer to fix.
cycle.for_you: Swing: take or protect the energy gains today. Puts: one idea, APH Dec 18 $72.50; the bar is the 4.927% 10 year. Long term: calm names inside their zones are APH, MSFT and COF; buy only small and after Wednesday.
